accused_occupation: Businessman (shopkeeper), per the defence version; the Court did not separately find this
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (Manoj, husband); in-laws (father-in-law Jamnadas, mother-in-law Dhanwantari)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.34 (conviction for appellants); charged also under IPC s.201, s.304-B and s.498-A, with the latter heads ending in acquittal
weapon: Hard and sharp object (knives and scissors were sent for examination)
evidence_type: Eyewitness (PW1-PW5 saw body being thrown); circumstantial chain; medical (autopsy and PW15 testimony); forensic (blood stains in house, blood on nails of co-accused)
aggravating_circumstances: Brutal murder of a young bride within six months of marriage; body cut into two pieces and dumped in a park
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of murder with common intention (IPC s.302/34); life imprisonment and fine of Rs.5000 each (default one year rigorous imprisonment); other charges ended in acquittal
high_court_outcome: Appeals dismissed; conviction and sentence upheld (judgment dated 23.8.2012)
offence_finally_established: Murder with common intention (IPC s.302 r/w s.34)
neutral_facts: The victim, a young woman married about six months earlier, lived in the house of the accused together with her husband, father-in-law, mother-in-law, a brother-in-law and a minor sister-in-law. On 16 September 2006 the police control room received a call that a middle-aged woman on a scooty had thrown two bundles wrapped in bed sheets into a park, with blood stains visible. Four men near the park had earlier seen a bundle with blood spots, and later saw a woman on an activa throw another packet and leave. The bundles contained the victim's body, which had been cut into two pieces. The autopsy recorded twelve ante mortem injuries, including defence wounds on the hands, and post-mortem cuts dividing the body. Death was due to shock and haemorrhage from multiple injuries. The medical evidence indicated that one person alone could not have inflicted them. Police searching the accused's house found blood stains, which were sampled. Blood was found on the fingernails of the mother-in-law but not on the nails of the husband or father-in-law. The accused's family claimed that the victim had gone to a relative's place and never returned home. No report of a homicidal death was lodged by the accused. Police registered a case against unknown persons and later filed a charge sheet against the four family members.
physical_harm: Death of the victim by shock and haemorrhage from twelve ante mortem injuries; body cut into two pieces post-mortem; defence wounds on hands
number_of_offences: 4 charged (s.302 r/w s.34, s.201, s.304-B, s.498-A); 1 finally upheld (s.302 r/w s.34)
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness evidence of PW1-PW5; autopsy report and PW15 testimony; blood stains in the house; blood on the mother-in-law's nails; the accused's false explanation under s.313 CrPC
witness_credibility: PW1-PW5 accepted as seeing the body being thrown; PW32 (minor sister-in-law) declared hostile and given no role; autopsy and PW15 evidence accepted as reliable
post_offence_conduct: No police report of the homicidal death lodged; false explanation given in statements under s.313 CrPC that the victim had gone to a relative's place and was missing
custody_duration: Not stated (arrest on 19.9.2006 only; duration not given)
trial_duration: offence: 16.09.2006; trial judgment: not given (sentence order dated 24.8.2009); High Court: 23.08.2012; Supreme Court: 29.06.2016
legal_representation: Accused: Sushil Kumar Jain, Sr. Adv. with others; State of M.P.: C.D. Singh, Sandeepan Pathak and others
investigation_status: FIR/crime registered 17.9.2006 against unknown persons; house searched and blood samples taken; charge sheet filed against four accused; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302/34 (life). High Court: appeals dismissed (23.8.2012). Supreme Court: appeals of the two accused dismissed; mother-in-law's SLP withdrawn
prosecution_argument: Section 106 Evidence Act applies because the facts are within the accused's special knowledge; the defence story is a blatant false plea completing the chain
defence_argument: Right to silence (Selvi) bars adverse inference; alibi that the accused were in the shop; no blood on appellants' nails; no specific evidence against them; Tomaso Bruno and Rajkumar cited
legal_principle_applied: Five-point circumstantial evidence test (Sharad Birdhichand Sarda); s.106 Evidence Act lighter burden for offences inside a house; false explanation as additional link; common intention
precedent_relied_upon: Sharad Birdhichand Sarda (1984) 4 SCC 116; Trimukh Maroti Kirkan (2006) 10 SCC 681; Kuldeep Singh (2000) 5 SCC 7; Rumi Bora Dutta (2013) 7 SCC 417; Suresh v. State of Haryana (2015) 2 SCC 227; State of W.B. v. Mir Mohammad Omar (2000) 8 SCC 382
judicial_aggravating_factors: Brutal murder of a young bride, body dismembered and disposed of; multiple injuries requiring more than one assailant
